The entry accurately represents the sequential stages of aerobic cellular respiration in eukaryotes as detailed in Topic 3.5 (specifically 3.5.A.3 and 3.5.B.1 through 3.5.B.5). The locations (cytosol, mitochondrion, mitochondrial matrix, inner mitochondrial membrane) and the inputs/outputs of each stage are perfectly aligned with the CED's Essential Knowledge statements.

The sequence follows 3.5.B.1–3.5.B.5: glycolysis forms ATP, NADH, and pyruvate; pyruvate moves to the mitochondrion for oxidation; the Krebs cycle occurs in the matrix; electrons carried by NADH and FADH2 enter the ETC; and the resulting proton gradient drives ATP formation. The CED identifies oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor in aerobic respiration (3.5.A.3) and calls ATP formation through chemiosmosis oxidative phosphorylation (3.5.A.3). Topic 3.5 requires this content. The wording needs no caution.

a_factual: Each item matches the CED. Item 1 matches 3.5.B.1 (glycolysis releases energy to form ATP, NADH from NAD+, and pyruvate). Item 2 matches 3.5.B.2 (pyruvate moves from the cytosol to the mitochondrion, where oxidation occurs). Item 3 matches 3.5.B.3 (Krebs cycle releases CO2, synthesizes ATP, and transfers electrons to NAD+ and FAD). Item 4 matches 3.5.A.3 i-ii and 3.5.B.4 (NADH and FADH2 deliver electrons through the ETC in the inner mitochondrial membrane to oxygen, the terminal acceptor, forming a proton gradient). Item 5 matches 3.5.A.3 iii (chemiosmosis through ATP synthase drives ATP formation, known as oxidative phosphorylation). The order matches the CED sequence 3.5.B.1 to 3.5.B.5 with 3.5.A.3. Minor note: the ced_evidence field puts a quotation in quote marks that is not verbatim. This does not change the body's factual accuracy. b_topic_codes: 3.5 is the topic whose objectives (3.5.A, 3.5.B) require this sequence, and no other topic codes are listed. c_ced_required: learning objective 3.5.B ('Explain how cells obtain energy from biological macromolecules') and essential knowledge 3.5.B.1-3.5.B.5 require a student to explain these stages in order. d_caution: the item wording uses the CED's own terms ('Krebs (citric acid) cycle', 'electron transport chain', 'oxidative phosphorylation'), so the point-earning wording is preserved and no caution is needed. Note that 'glycolysis (cytosol)' is inferred from 3.5.B.2 ('transported from the cytosol') rather than stated outright, which is acceptable.
